name: NativeLedger
subtitle: Automatic app update ledger
description:
NativeLedger keeps an automatic, tamper evident ledger of app updates for a folder you choose. Watch your Applications folder, and NativeLedger records a dated entry each time an app in it changes. You can also add a single app with the file picker.

Each entry records the bundle identifier, version, build, architecture slices, minimum system version, signing identifier, signing team and declared entitlements. It records the code directory hash and the SHA-256 of the main executable. It lists the privacy usage descriptions, the update feed address and the background items by name. Background items are login items, launch agents, launch daemons, XPC services and helpers inside the app. Each entry also stores the result of the macOS code signing validity check.

NativeLedger flags changes that a version number does not show. A silent rebuild means the executable or code directory hash changed while the version and build stayed the same. A version regression means the version went down. A team change means the signing team changed. NativeLedger also flags a new background item, a new privacy usage description, an invalid signature and a changed update feed. New entitlements and architecture changes are marked as well. Recent changes lists the entries of the last seven days from all ledgers.

Each entry stores the SHA-256 of the entry before it. Verify chain recalculates every hash and names the earliest entry that does not match. An edited, removed or reordered earlier entry breaks the chain. Exported copies cover the newest entries. Acknowledge accepts the latest entry as your reviewed baseline. The acknowledgement is itself an entry in the chain.

Export Ledger saves a .nativeledger file in a place you choose. The file contains no file paths and no saved access. On another Mac, Compare with Ledger File opens that file and compares the newest entry for each app. You see Same build, Different binary for the same version, Different version, Only on this Mac or Only on the other Mac.

Alerts are optional and off by default. When you turn them on, NativeLedger shows a local notification for an invalid signature, a team change or a new background item.

Know the limits. NativeLedger records changes while it is open. When you open it again, it records what changed while it was closed. It reads the folders and apps you choose and nothing else. The signature check uses the macOS code signing check. A valid result means the app matches its signature. It is not malware detection and not a safety verdict. NativeLedger does not inspect the code inside nested items, effective permissions or network traffic. It does not download or install updates.

Everything stays on your Mac. NativeLedger makes no network connections and has no account and no analytics. Sample shows synthetic ledgers that are kept in memory and never saved.
promotional_text: Watch a folder and NativeLedger records each app update in a hash chained ledger. Spot silent rebuilds, team changes, new background items and invalid signatures.
whats_new: Build 4 is a new design. NativeLedger keeps an automatic, tamper evident update ledger for folders you choose. Entries now include background items, privacy usage descriptions, the update feed and a signature validity check. New anomaly flags, Recent changes, optional alerts, chain verification and comparison across Mac computers are included.
